newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close weaker in quiet dealings.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close weaker in quiet dealings.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker on Monday, following U.S. treasuries lower, with trading very light amid a lack of significant economic news or data, analysts said.

"There's not many people around, so the market hasn't been too active, at least not until two o'clock when the U.S. market came off," said David Yu, a fixed-income portfolio manager with Perigee Investment Counsel Inc.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.34 to C$116.79 to yield 6.694 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 12/32 to yield 6.69 percent. The bonds traded to yield at par, compared with Friday when there was a spread of one basis point.

"We're just being dragged lower by treasuries. Flows were a little bit better on the sell side but very, very light," said one bond trader. "The market is trading a little bit long and this fear of potentially Japan selling some of its holdings in treasuries has the market a little bit nervous."
Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets fell after Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said stable exchange rates were critical to Japan maintaining its holdings of U.S. bonds.

Analysts said the market was now looking ahead to a report on U.S. durable goods orders out on Wednesday. Beyond that the market was already anticipating the meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee on July 1.
In ratings news, Dominion Bond Rating Service confirmed the ratings of the province of Manitoba's long-term debt at A and short-term debt at R-1 (low) with stable trends.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.43 to C$108.18 to yield 6.136 percent, compared to its U.S. equivalent, which fell 7/32 to yield 6.41 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 27 basis points from 30 basis points at Friday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 2.81 percent against its U.S. equivalent, which yielded 5.15 percent.
